name: Varo

anatomy.part: the boatman's head, inside the round head just above the chin
his hip, where the torso meets the legs
his elbow, at the bend of the outstretched arm
the shell coin in his open palm, at the end of the forearm
the bow tip of the hull, where his feet stand on the top edge
the keel at the bottom of the hull
the lower curve of the stern, where the hull sweeps up from the keel
the stern rising toward the post

myth: When Aun cut the string, the first things to drift past the last lamp were the drowned, and none of them knew the way. A boatman of the Upper Sea, grey-bearded and thin as a gutting knife, took a shell coin from a drowned woman's hand and laid it on his palm. That was the fare. He rowed her out past the edge of the wind into the dark the Unflown keeps, and he has not yet given the coin back. Mother Hesk counts every string in Vel and has counted this one missing. Kael the Netter casts for the boat each night and brings up only weed. Tavo blows past the stern and laughs, because he cannot be bargained with and will not lift a boat for a coin. Sil looks down from her lamp at the drowned, searching among them for Aun. So the old ones say, mending nets: pay the fare when you are ready to be ferried, and never ask the boatman for change.
verse:
A shell on his palm
the fare for the dark crossing
still not given back
